Question for the C++ crowd: I'm a very rusty C++ user and am trying to dust off my skills and acquire more knowledge using the manual PPP (3rd edition). It relies heavily on the use of modules such as import std, and also at least one module that the author has written himself. I'm coding in Visual Studio 2026 and I've already stubbed my toe on this module business several times. It's been set-up stuff so far and not insurmountable, and at the worst I can no doubt manage for a while using include<iostream> and so on, but it's annoying. I see there are quite a few people on the help sites muttering darkly about modules - which according to them have not bedded in as well as expected - and saying learners should avoid having anything to do with them. 

So my question is: is this true? Should I dump PPP and find another manual that is less fixated on modules? And if so, which one? 

Basically I'm trying to ascertain just HOW bad the level of inconvenience is, because there's always some kind of framework bullshit when you're starting on a language, so I don't want to give up unless it's going to be really bad.
